title: cvassure assurance finding
description: One statement about one asset, from one check, at one access tier. Every detector in cvassure returns a list of these and nothing else; the report, the scoring harness and the audit log all consume this one shape.

finding_id.description: Unique id for this finding. Stable across a run, not across runs.

asset_ref.description: What this finding is about: an image path, a contributor id, 'model', or a receipt reference.

asset_type.description: Which kind of thing asset_ref names.

attack_class.description: The attack this finding would be evidence of, if true.

access_tier.description: The access level the audit was granted: 0 answers only, 1 plus weights, 2 plus internals.

raw_score.description: How suspicious the asset is, 0..1, higher is worse. A ranking, not a probability.

calibrated_score.description: raw_score mapped to an actual probability of being poisoned, when a calibration split was available. Null during a live audit, where there is no ground truth.

confidence.description: How sure we are of this finding, 0..1 — a different question from raw_score. A hash mismatch is confidence 1.0; a statistical shape argument is around 0.45 however alarming the score.

severity.description: Graded from the score, for triage.

reason.description: One human-readable sentence containing real numbers. Enforced: a finding whose reason contains jargon or no number is rejected at construction.

evidence.description: Detector-specific supporting values behind the reason.

artefacts.description: Paths to images produced as evidence, such as a saliency heatmap or a reconstructed trigger.

limitations.description: What this particular assessment could not establish.

unavailable_reason.description: Set when the check could not run at all. Such a finding is a status message, not a claim: its raw_score is always 0 and must not be scored.
